headline.caveat: Price undisclosed. 20-year agreement for 1,121MW of Clinton (IL) nuclear output from June 2027, incl. a ~30MW uprate.

realized_to_date.caveat: Deliveries under the agreement begin June 2027, when Illinois' zero-emission-credit support for Clinton expires.

nature_md: Meta's first nuclear deal: a 20-year attribute-and-energy purchase covering 1,121MW from Constellation's Clinton Clean Energy Center in Illinois starting June 2027, timed to replace the expiring state ZEC program that had kept the plant open. Includes a ~30MW plant uprate. Meta buys the clean-energy attributes to match its regional data-center load; the plant continues serving the local grid. Effectively a solvency guarantee for a plant that had been slated for early retirement.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Meta books nothing until June 2027, then power/attribute costs as data-center opex; commitment disclosed among purchase obligations, off balance sheet.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Constellation replaces expiring state ZEC subsidy revenue with contracted corporate revenue from mid-2027; supported license extension and uprate capex at Clinton.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** private AI demand seamlessly replaces a public subsidy — the cleanest case of hyperscaler money keeping existing nuclear online. **Bear:** with the price confidential, ratepayer advocates cannot verify whether Meta pays more or less than the ZEC support it replaces, and grid consumers keep the reliability externalities either way.
